orbitalInsight.title: Hormuz shifts from pure disruption toward contested reopening
orbitalInsight.summary: Reported mine-clearing of the main shipping lane and renewed Iran-Oman corridor negotiations reduce immediate navigational risk, but transit remains politically and militarily conditional rather than normalized.
orbitalInsight.delta: Supersede the binary open/closed model with a state transition: severe disruption -> partially demined / negotiated corridor -> contested reopening. Physical throughput and freight/insurance data must confirm the transition before confidence rises further.
firstOrderImpacts: lower near-term oil risk premium
potential improvement in tanker throughput
possible easing in freight and insurance stress
secondOrderImpacts: reduced energy-inflation pressure if physical flows recover
lower tail-risk premium in rates and risk assets
greater value of real-time vessel-flow validation versus political statements

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Independent physical-flow data will confirm or reject the claimed reopening faster and more reliably than official political statements or oil-price reaction alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: Official mine-clearing / corridor statements plus Brent price reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: Independent vessel counts/throughput, freight rates, war-risk insurance, and later refined-product delivery data
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: Forecast error for 3-7 day confirmed throughput and freight/insurance normalization versus the baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the added complexity if public/low-cost physical-flow data cannot beat the baseline on held-out outcomes or arrives too late to change a decision.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Qatar PM meets Iranian foreign minister in Tehran
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source says the meeting focused on de-escalation and creating conditions for dialogue, and confirms ongoing discussion of a temporary Hormuz corridor and joint mine clearing.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: oil reverses higher after White House says no U.S.-Iran talks are happening
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports the White House said no U.S.-Iran negotiations are underway, despite Qatar's mediation effort; oil rose as markets reduced the probability of near-term diplomatic normalization.

contradictingEvidence.title: Qatar primary source confirms active mediation and a dialogue-enabling effort
contradictingEvidence.note: Active mediation means diplomatic channels are not closed; the White House statement should therefore be interpreted as absence of direct U.S.-Iran negotiations, not absence of diplomacy.

alphaHunter.falsifier: Upgrade from MEDIATION_ACTIVE / DIRECT_TALKS_ABSENT if the White House, U.S. State Department, Iranian Foreign Ministry, or Qatar publishes primary evidence that direct U.S.-Iran negotiations have begun. Downgrade the mediation channel if Qatar or Iran says the initiative has stalled or the Hormuz corridor framework is abandoned.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters Open Interest: Asia crude imports remain well below pre-conflict levels
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters cites Kpler estimates of 23.12 million b/d of Asian crude arrivals in August versus 26.91 million b/d pre-conflict; Kpler tracked only 2.3 million b/d of August crude exports through Hormuz versus 15.82 million b/d in the three months before the war.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: oil prices rise as negotiations stall and flows remain restricted
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports that restricted flows and lack of diplomatic progress are pushing traders to reassess earlier reopening optimism.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: delivery lag can delay downstream confirmation
contradictingEvidence.note: The same analysis notes that if Middle East exports accelerated only in early August, some cargoes may not arrive in Japan, South Korea or China until September, so August import data may understate a very recent recovery.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: visible vessel traffic improved modestly to 10 transits Wednesday
contradictingEvidence.note: Short-term vessel counts show positive momentum even though absolute throughput and downstream arrivals remain far below pre-conflict levels.

alphaHunter.falsifier: Downgrade the measurement-conflict thesis if September Asian crude arrivals materially rebound toward pre-conflict levels, Kpler-observed Hormuz exports converge upward with official U.S. recovery claims, and freight/insurance/product-market indicators normalize consistently with those higher flows.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Shipping traffic through Strait of Hormuz rises slightly
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports Kpler tracked 10 commodity-vessel transits Wednesday, up from eight Tuesday, still below the roughly 15-vessel 10-day average.

supportingEvidence.title: Oman: temporary maritime corridor coordinated with IMO
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Omani material confirms a real navigation-restoration mechanism exists and emphasizes freedom of navigation without transit fees.

supportingEvidence.title: IMO: confirmed Middle East maritime incidents
supportingEvidence.note: IMO continues to list recent vessel damage in and near Hormuz, showing physical-security risk has not disappeared merely because traffic is rising.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters/Kpler: traffic remains below recent average and AIS coverage is incomplete
contradictingEvidence.note: The same report says traffic remains below the recent moving average and acknowledges that transponder-off vessels can be missed.

contradictingEvidence.title: IMO: recent confirmed vessel damage remains part of the operating environment
contradictingEvidence.note: Recent confirmed maritime incidents mean a higher vessel count is not equivalent to restored physical security.

alphaHunter.falsifier: Upgrade toward NORMALIZING only if several consecutive days of independent vessel and oil-flow data move materially toward pre-war baselines while maritime incidents, tanker freight and war-risk insurance also normalize. Downgrade the recovery-momentum thesis if traffic falls back toward crisis lows or renewed attacks reverse the increase.
alphaHunter.hypothesis: Combining pre-war absolute-flow baselines with daily vessel momentum and maritime-security telemetry will classify Hormuz recovery earlier and more accurately than diplomacy headlines or Brent/WTI alone.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Qatar PM heads to Tehran as Hormuz flows remain at a three-month low
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports Qatar's prime minister will visit Tehran to relaunch diplomacy and cites ship-tracking data showing about 5 million b/d of Hormuz oil flow on Monday versus roughly 20 million b/d before the war.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: support for temporary corridor, mine clearing and freedom of navigation
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source confirms support for Iran-Oman corridor and mine-clearing talks and explicitly calls for freedom of maritime navigation.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: phased Hormuz framework remains under discussion
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source confirms ongoing Oman-Iran discussions on a phased temporary navigation route and joint demining project rather than a completed normalization state.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: oil prices continue falling as markets price reopening hopes
contradictingEvidence.note: Brent and WTI continued multi-day declines, showing that market pricing is moving toward de-escalation even though observed physical flow remains deeply impaired.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: Iran retains military leverage and negotiations remain unresolved
contradictingEvidence.note: The same report says Iran retains missile/drone capability, 70 maritime incidents have been recorded since the war began, and no final Iran-Oman agreement exists yet.

alphaHunter.falsifier: Downgrade the current narrative-physical divergence if independent Hormuz oil flow rises and holds near the pre-war ~20 million b/d baseline, maritime incidents fall materially, freight/war-risk insurance normalizes, and Iran/Oman/Qatar publish compatible navigation terms that are operationally observed.
